result.title: Leaderboard Hacking: Preference-Based Model Evaluations are Vulnerable to Manipulation
result.summary: Arena-style rankings of language models are a widely used evaluation framework in online leaderboards, research papers, and model evaluation in production. These rankings aim to realistically assess model performance using pairwise comparisons of anonymous models on user prompts, aggregating votes via the Bradley-Terry model to produce the final ranking. However, we find that these leaderboards are highly vulnerable to several manipulation strategies that unscrupulous providers could use to boost a model's rank: strategic voting (individual votes that boost a model's rank, including votes on irrelevant models), strategic prompting (choosing prompts that favor a model), and strategic nomination (boosting the rank of a model by inserting irrelevant models). We demonstrate these effects on public leaderboard data, analyze the circumstances that cause these vulnerabilities, and describe approaches to safeguard against each attack. Notably, these issues hold for any preference-based evaluation using the Bradley-Terry model that allows open prompting, voting, or model submission. These manipulations boost the rank of nearly every tested model; each attack can boost a model by up to 15-20 places in a ranking and, combined, they can boost a model by up to 45 places.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文研究 arena 式语言模型排行榜的脆弱性，展示策略性投票、策略性提示与策略性提名三类操纵手段可在 Bradley-Terry 偏好聚合下把模型排名提升 15–20 位（组合可达 45 位），并分析成因与防护措施。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文关注的是偏好投票与排名聚合机制被博弈操纵的问题，不涉及视觉信息是否进入内部状态、latent 推理状态生成/更新、证据获取或停止决策，也未提供可迁移到 LVR 的训练或方法线索，故与当前研究主线缺少实质联系。
